text:
kevin_sales: FYI - MetroConnect POC demo tomorrow AM. They asked for an "assurance bundle" to review during the session. Ask list: SOC 2 Type II excerpt (control summary + date range), ISO 27001 scope statement, Annex A control mapping (top-level), full subprocessor list (redacted contacts ok), a short encryption/key-management attestation, and a "pen-test / red-team letter" (they used that phrase). They also want a simple network diagram showing Hosted vs Dedicated deployment, and a delta on Dedicated pricing if we enable single-tenant burst. Can we get these by EOD Thu?

kevin_se: Do we know topology for the POC? Hosted sandbox or Dedicated in-customer-VPC? The network diagram and k8s/NSG notes will differ a lot. Also who at MetroConnect is the technical lead?

kevin_sales: Starting on Redwood-hosted sandbox. They'll only spin Dedicated if perf/SLA looks good in POC. Tech lead is alex.mullen@metroconnect.net (Alex M, Head of Platform).

rachel_security: We can assemble the bundle. What we can provide off-the-shelf: SOC 2 Type II excerpt (summary + auditor assertion), ISO 27001 scope statement, a one-page Annex A mapping for controls we cover, and the subprocessors CSV with redactions. For encryption/KMS attestation we can provide a short note describing CMK usage, envelope encryption, and key rotation cadence.

Regarding "pen-test / red-team letter" — we have 3 options:
1) Customer accepts our standard attestation letter confirming periodic internal red-team and vulnerability scanning (fast, no cost).
2) Customer requests a third-party pen-test attestation naming our assessor — Legal + a PO required; we schedule with assessor (timeline ~7-12 business days, potential fee).
3) Customer runs their own scanner against a scoped staging endpoint using ephemeral creds (fastest for POC).
Pick which they'd prefer.

igor_infra: For the scanner approach we typically provide either a) presigned S3 for scan payloads or b) short-lived STS role for pull/push operations. Examples:
- presign (2h):
```
aws s3 presign s3://redwood-poc-staging/metro-scan.tar.gz --expires-in 7200
```
- assume-role (1h):
```
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/MetroPOCScanner --role-session-name metro-scan --duration-seconds 3600
```
Both require an IP allowlist and a preferred user-agent string so we can validate traffic. We can also issue a short-lived KMS data key via GenerateDataKey for envelope encryption if they want to upload encrypted payloads (we never hand out long-lived KMS plaintext keys).

igor_infra: Note on pricing delta: enabling single-tenant burst for Dedicated typically adds a 12-18% uplift on top of the reserved node rate for that pool depending on instance type. I can run a quick calc if we know target peak RPS and desired burst headroom.

doc-bot: Draft assurance bundle uploaded: https://internal.redwood/s3/assurance/1829997766-metroconnect-draft.zip (SOC excerpt, ISO scope, subprocessors.csv, draft diagram).

sophie_legal: We can sign our standard attestation immediately (no PO). If MetroConnect insists on a pen-test letter naming a vendor, Legal needs: PO, scope, and indemnity clause confirmation. We'll coordinate with the assessor. Expect ~7-12 business days once PO accepted. Also confirm we don't disclose assessor contact details until they've agreed to the scope.

rachel_security: Action items for fast turn: 1) Sales confirm whether they want our attestation or a third-party letter; 2) If they want scanning, provide IP ranges + scan window + user-agent; 3) If they want price calc, provide expected peak tokens/sec or concurrency target. I'll prep the Annex A mapping and encryption attestation ASAP (ETA 1 business day).

kevin_sales: I'll message Alex right now for: preferred attestation type, IP ranges + preferred scan window (dates/times), and target concurrency for pricing. Will update here once Alex replies. Thanks all :thumbsup:
